bugs: Guest request to /api/posts without an Accept: application/json header returns 500 (Route [login] not defined). The auth middleware tries to redirect to a login route that doesn't exist, and bootstrap/app.php has no redirectGuestsTo/shouldRenderJsonWhen for api/*
No PATCH route (routes/api.php:9). Partial updates only work over PUT, and PATCH /api/posts/{id} returns 405
Empty query filters (?status=&tag=&per_page=) return 422 instead of being treated as absent, because the IndexPostRequest rules are not nullable
Tag creation uses firstOrCreate (Post.php:55), which can race against the unique index on tags.name; createOrFirst handles that
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:36 — ->response()->setStatusCode(201) is unnecessary ceremony; a resource wrapping a wasRecentlyCreated model already returns 201
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:21,25 — reads $request->enum()/integer() from raw input instead of validated() data, so filtering is decoupled from what was validated
database/factories/PostFactory.php:17 — the definition has no user_id, so Post::factory()->create() fails unless ->for() is chained
app/Policies/PostPolicy.php:17 — duplicates the update logic instead of delegating (trivial)
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:206 — asserts a model scope directly inside an HTTP index test, which mixes levels
strengths: Thin controller using $request->user()->posts() scoping, safe()->except('tags'), when() filters and withQueryString pagination
Modern model: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy] and #[Scope] attributes, a casts() method, a backed enum for status
Authorization at route level via ->can() with a policy that uses $post->user()->is($user)
Observer handles the unique slug and sets published_at only when it is missing
Solid tests: guests, validation, 403 for a non-author including when the payload is invalid, 404, tag dedupe/trim, filters, pagination

bugs: Minor: the slug uniqueness check in the observer (exists() loop) is check-then-insert, so concurrent creates with the same title could hit the unique constraint. impl-1 has the same issue
antipatterns: routes/api.php:9-10 — separate put and patch route lines (and no named routes) where Route::match(['put','patch']) or apiResource()->only() would be tidier
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:20 — PostStatus::from() on the validated string; $request->enum() would be shorter
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:21 — Http::preventStrayRequests() in a suite that makes no HTTP calls is noise
strengths: Handles guest API requests without a JSON header correctly via redirectGuestsTo returning null for api/* (verified: 401, not 500), with a test for it
Supports both PUT and PATCH, and route-model binding by slug
Validation uses 'sometimes','required' for partial updates, a nullable index filter so empty query params are treated as absent (tested), and required tags.* entries
Uses createOrFirst for tags, which is safe against the unique index, plus trim/filter/uniqueStrict
Same modern model idioms: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope], enum cast, whereRelation; the policy delegates delete to update
Factory includes a user_id default and a published() state
Thorough tests: published_at kept across draft→published toggles with time travel, empty filters, combined filters, pagination, 403 even with an invalid body, cascade of pivot rows on delete

v.rationale: Both implementations are structurally almost identical: an observer for the slug and published_at, a policy enforced through route-level ->can(), Form Requests, an API Resource that plucks tag names, #[Scope] scopes and attribute-based models. Both suites pass (impl-2 26/26, impl-1 22/22). The probes are what separate them. impl-1 returns a 500 to a guest calling GET /api/posts without an Accept: application/json header, because auth tries to redirect to a login route that doesn't exist. It also has no PATCH route (405), and it rejects empty query filters with a 422. impl-2 handles all three correctly: 401, PATCH works, and empty filters are ignored. impl-2 also uses createOrFirst, which is safe when two requests create the same tag at once, puts a user_id default in the factory, skips the redundant setStatusCode(201), filters from validated() data, and has broader edge-case tests. impl-2's weaknesses are small (put and patch declared as separate route lines, a little test noise), so it ranks first.
